key_insight: UnDA transfers useful structure between imaging modalities without paired data by aligning semantically meaningful class tokens and down-weighting uncertain predictions.
clinical_relevance: This could improve segmentation performance when paired multimodal scans are unavailable, potentially making cross-modal models more practical in real-world medical imaging workflows.
method: Alignment Module: attention-based pooling extracts class tokens in a backbone-agnostic way.
UCT-OT: uncertainty-weighted optimal transport suppresses noisy feature alignment from low-confidence predictions.
ProtoNCE: per-class prototype memory encourages stable, globally discriminative representations across unpaired batches.
evidence_signal: In strictly unpaired segmentation evaluations, the method consistently improved accuracy and boundary precision in the target modality.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reliable uncertainty estimates and careful tuning of alignment/prototype components when modality gaps are large.
paper_title: UnDA: Unpaired Domain Alignment for Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer in Medical Imaging
